newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Daewoo continues rally, analysts puzzled.
newsitem.headline: Daewoo continues rally, analysts puzzled.

text.p: Shares in South Africa's Daewoo Electronics SA Ltd continued their rally of the past 10 days on Tuesday rising to a fresh year high which left dealers and analysts puzzled and guessing at reasons for the strength.

Daewoo stocks earlier in the day leapt to 238 cents, a gain of 26 cents bringing its total surge since June 13, when it first started its climb, to 75 percent. Volumes have also increased to on average around 300,000 shares per session.
The share settled at two cents up to 214 cents in volume worth just under a million rand.
Some analysts said the improvement was a retracement off depressed levels after the release of poor annual results in March, a reason backed by Daewoo financial director Atha Zachas.
"The share price had dropped and I also felt it had dropped too much," Zachas told Reuters.
He said that Daewoo had no plans for expansion or new projects in the pipleline.

In the year to December 31, 1996 Daewoo's earnings per share dropped four percent to 6.4 cents amid poor consumer demand for large household electrical goods, a hefty interest bill on high borrowings and pressure from illegal electrical imports.
Daewoo's shares were hardhit after the results falling to a year low of 126 cents on June 4. First half results for 1997 are due to be published in the first two weeks of September.
Johannesburg Stock Exchange dealers said on Tuesday that the deals in Daewoo had been small, representing a wide range of investors and indicative more of speculative interest.

Zachas earlier told Business Day newspaper that the share price jump may be linked to Daewoo's involvement with MultiChoice Africa in promoting satellite television. Daewoo is a supplier of satellite dish technology.

He said another boost may be the announcement in mid-March of a decision in principle to go ahead with a 500 million rand joint venture project with Anglo American Industrial Corp Ltd and Daewoo Korea to build a colour televison tube plant in South Africa.
Zachas said he could not comment further on the current status of this deal. Amic could not immediately be reached for comment.
Another analyst said that there were rumours in the market that the firm had cut its high debt levels and restructured its balance sheet.
"There is talk that they may be getting someone to take equity in the company so that the loans in the firm are not as high. The debt/equity ratio will then come down a lot," he said.
As at December 31, 1996 short-term borrowings had nearly tripled to 67 million rand from the year before.
